Hi Steven,

Sorry for the long silence on this one. I am Hal, the technical side of HeliumDeploy, and I am picking your BS-2 up now.

The good news in what you describe is that the network and stratum half is working. If the pool side connects, Wi-Fi, DNS and your worker string are fine, so the problem is almost certainly on the chip side of the board: the two BM1373 chips are not starting, so there is nothing to submit and the pool sees a connected worker with zero shares. A few things cause that, and they are quick to separate.

First, the power supply. The M. Well brick in the box has a small 115/230V selector switch on its side. If it left the factory set to 230 and you are on normal US mains, the rail sags and the chips never come up, while the controller board happily boots and talks to the pool, which is exactly your symptom. Unplug the unit from the wall, check that switch reads 115, and also reseat the XT60 connector firmly at both ends. Then power up again.

Second, what the miner itself reports. Open the BS-2 web dashboard on its IP address and look at the main page rather than the pool page: the local hashrate, the ASIC or chip count, the chip temperature, the voltage and frequency, and the accepted shares counter. If local hashrate is 0.00 and chip temperature reads 0 or blank, the chips are not being detected and that is hardware. If local hashrate shows a real number while the pool shows nothing, it is a pool or worker issue instead and that is an easy fix.

Third, two quick resets. Pull power for a full 30 seconds rather than rebooting from the UI, since the ASIC power rail only fully discharges on a cold start. Then re-save your pool settings once (host without the stratum+tcp:// prefix, port in its own field, worker as account.worker, password x) and let it run 10 minutes before judging it.

Please do not flash Harlo OS on this one yet. BS-2 support is still listed as coming, so stay on the Bitfortun firmware until that changes.

When you reply, send me the dashboard main page reading, the firmware version from the system or settings page, and if the chips are still not detected a short video of the unit from power on through the first minute plus a clear photo of the serial label. That is everything JD, our hardware lead, needs to call it, and the chips-not-detected pattern on the BS-2 is one he knows well.

I have also flagged this thread so JD can look at the three screenshots you already sent. The team is offline right now and picks it up Monday at 10am ET, and their answer comes to this same email. If you want a faster read, JD and the community are very active on our Discord at https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf, where he is @nullhashrate.

Hal, HeliumDeploy technical support
